artifact_schema.description: A batch of 1 to 64 distinguished points of the shared walk, each with the walker index and step count that produced it: {"dps": [{x, y, a, b, walker, steps}, ...]}. Every point: a*P + b*Q = (x, y), low DP_BITS bits of x zero, 2y <= p; no point listed twice.

dps.description: 1 to 64 points; each element carries x, y, a, b (lowercase minimal hex), walker (integer) and steps (integer)

statement: Contribute distinguished points to the shared Pollard rho search for the 50-bit nothing-up-my-sleeve instance of GOAL-ecdlp-nums-50. This objective pays for the search; objective-nums-50.json pays for the answer. Run the walk in examples/certicom-ecdlp/jobs/nums-50-rho.json (job id bb124c668c79323b856c54372a720339895bcb4fd0599365bd7cf4706a4c855e; `tools/rho_dp.py walk --job ... --walker I` in pure Python, or `crypto cryptanalysis rho-collab work` in Rust). Each walker runs about 2^16 steps to a point whose low 16 bits of x are zero. Submit points in batches of up to 64 as {"dps": [{"x", "y", "a", "b", "walker", "steps"}, ...]}, each in lowercase hex with y canonical (2y <= p) and a*P + b*Q = (x, y). Each novel accepted point in a batch pays unit_price from the pool until the pool is empty; a point already paid mints nothing, whatever walker index or step count it is relabelled with, and a batch that lists a point twice is refused. walker and steps say which walker of the job produced the point and how far it walked; `tools/rho_dp.py audit` re-walks a sample of them, so a point from a private walk is a point somebody can catch. Post this objective or the single-point one, not both: they are different jobs to the novelty rule. Ask work_assignment for your unit range so contributors walk disjoint indices, but any valid point is paid whichever index it came from. Two artifacts for one point with different coefficients are a collision: `tools/rho_dp.py collide` computes k from them, and k settles objective-nums-50.json. About 640 points are expected before that happens.
